title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Longue Marche notes, cote 149). For a morphism f: X -> Y of connected (étale-)homotopy objects, Grothendieck works with a 'relative fundamental group' E_{X/Y}. It is defined with respect to a 'base point' T, which can be a pro-object, a universal covering or a geometric point. In modern terms E^T_{X/Y} is the kernel of pi_1(X,T) -> pi_1(Y,T), or the fundamental group of the homotopy fibre.

Previous page. The map X -> Y factors canonically (eq. 14) as X -> Y' -> Y, with Y' finite étale or pro-finite-étale over Y. This is the étale analogue of the Stein factorisation on the pi_0 / pi_1 level: Y' is the cover corresponding to the image of pi_1(X) in pi_1(Y). After the factorisation, pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y') is an epimorphism. Then E^T_{X/Y} ≅ E^T_{X/Y'} (eq. 15), so one reduces to the surjective case. He then warns about the difference between X_T and X ×_{Y'} T.

This page.
- Let X~ and Y~ be the universal covers of X and Y deduced from T~ and T -> Y. Consider the diagram X <- X_{Y~} <- X~ <- Z over Y' <- Y~ <- Y.
- Eq. (17): E^T_{X/Y} ≅ E^{X~}_{X/Y} ≅ Ker(pi_1(X,X~) -> pi_1(Y,Y~)). The relative group, computed with base point T, equals the one computed with the universal-cover base point, and equals the kernel of the induced map of profinite fundamental groups. This uses the homotopy exact sequence and the identification E^Z_{X_{Y~}} ≅ E^{X~}_{X_{Y~}}.
- A general formula (18) was started and then crossed out.
- Second interpretation. Take T to be a geometric point xi_x of X, with image xi_y in Y. Let X_{xi_y} be the geometric fibre, so xi_x is a geometric point of that fibre. Eq. (19): E^{xi_x}_{X/Y} ≅ pi_1(X_{xi_y}, xi_x). So E_{X/Y} is the fundamental group of the geometric fibres.

Next page. Compatibility with an earlier description (11), via E^{xi_T} ≅ E^T (eq. 20). He stresses that E_{X/Y} is a diagram (local system) of profinite groups and isomorphisms indexed by base points. It is not merely an outer group: the transition isomorphisms are genuinely specified, not only defined up to inner automorphisms.

Purpose. This sets up the relative / fibre fundamental group needed for the 'Longue Marche' analysis of fibrations, e.g. elementary fibrations of curves, through which pi_1 of higher-dimensional anabelian varieties is built from successive extensions.
errors: (19) is conditional. It identifies Ker(pi_1 X -> pi_1 Y) with pi_1 of the geometric fibre. In general, e.g. SGA1 X for proper separable morphisms with geometrically connected fibres, one only has exactness pi_1(F) -> pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y) -> 1. Injectivity on the left needs a fibration-type hypothesis, e.g. pi_2(Y)=0 (Y a K(pi,1)) or Artin elementary fibrations. The margin of the previous page ('hypothèse d'homotopie') suggests Grothendieck is assuming such a homotopy exact sequence, so this is a stated hypothesis rather than an error.
Formula (18) is crossed out and left incomplete; the 'cas général' formula is not actually written.

ideas.what: Canonical factorisation X -> Y' -> Y with Y' (pro-)finite étale over Y, making pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y') surjective, and reduction of relative pi_1 to that case
ideas.modern_name: étale (pi_1-)Stein factorisation / cover associated to the image subgroup
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (Stein factorisation, homotopy exact sequence X.1)

ideas.what: Relative fundamental group E_{X/Y} = Ker(pi_1 X -> pi_1 Y), independent of the choice of base point (T, universal cover, geometric point)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the homotopy fibre / relative fundamental group
ideas.where_published: SGA1 X (homotopy exact sequence); Esquisse d'un programme discusses fibrations of anabelian varieties

ideas.what: Identification of E_{X/Y} with pi_1 of geometric fibres, and its nature as a local system of profinite groups over the groupoid of base points rather than an outer group
ideas.modern_name: fibre fundamental group as a local system (functor on the fundamental groupoid); distinction between local system of groups and outer action
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 X; groupoid viewpoint in SGA1 V and later Deligne (several base points)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 X for the exact sequence; the explicit 'diagram of isomorphisms, not an outer group' remark is perhaps only in these notes

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working-out of the homotopy exact sequence and the base-point (in)dependence of the relative profinite fundamental group, all standard since SGA1. The care about 'diagram of isomorphisms vs outer group' is characteristic but not new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: In (17) the symbols read as 'ξ' inside Ker(...) are most likely the script E/ℰ used for fundamental groups: Ker(ℰ^{X~}_X -> ℰ^{Y~}_Y), i.e. Ker(pi_1(X,X~) -> pi_1(Y,Y~)), not geometric points.
The superscript in the first line of (17) is T (possibly with a dot/overline), consistent with ℰ^T_{X/Y}.
Line after (17): 'ℰ^Z_{X_{Y~}} ≅ ℰ^{X~}_{X_{Y~}}' with partly overwritten indices; (18) right-hand side is crossed out entirely.
'Une autre interprétation' (the struck word 'tra' is a false start).
